insights.title: LCS diff pipeline: reconcile same-filename pairs as Moved before replacement detection runs
insights.content: In the LCS-based diff pipeline in DiffService.ClassifyChanges, mods that appear in both the "removed" set and the "new" set under the same filename (i.e., swapped or reordered mods whose relative order inverted) must be pulled from both sets and emitted as Moved before the replacement-detection step runs. Without this pre-pass, swapped mods fall through all classification branches and are incorrectly emitted as Removed + Added pairs. The reconciliation pass is ~10 lines and runs in Step 2, before Step 3 builds the newByCurPos position dictionary for replacement matching. Scenarios 2, 10, and 14 in ScenarioTests validate this behavior. Any future modification to ClassifyChanges must preserve the ordering: reconciliation → replacement detection → Added/Inserted classification → dependent attribution.
insights.source: plan.md architecture section, WP-001 acceptance criteria, WP-002 ScenarioTests

insights.title: api-surface.md requires periodic cross-checks against the live public API to catch silent gaps
insights.content: The project-manifest api-surface.md document can silently fall out of sync with the actual public API without causing any build or test failure. During the 2026-07-21 LCS diff pipeline plan, HasIndependentMovedModsAsync (DiffService.cs L50, called by FileMonitoringCoordinator) was discovered to be entirely absent from api-surface.md — despite being a production entry point in active use. It was added in WP-003 as a pre-existing gap fix. Similarly, ReadModListAsync (added in WP-002) required a documentation catch-up pass. A periodic manual audit of api-surface.md against the actual public methods in DiffService.cs, FileService.cs, and other service classes would catch similar gaps before they accumulate. The audit is not automated and must be done by the Documentation or Planner agent.
insights.source: synthesis Gold Nugget #6, WP-003 documentation pipeline
